title: Woolworths Limited - proposed acquisition of Roger and Dale's IGA in Thurgoona
targets: Roger and Dales IGA in Thurgoona

timeline.event: ACCC commences review under Merger Review Process Guidelines.
ACCC announced it would not oppose the proposed acquisition.

body_sections.Summary: Woolworths proposes to acquire the liquor licence, goodwill, liquor stock, and the supermarket space of Roger & Dales IGA, Thurgoona, NSW.
body_sections.Market definition: For the purposes of this competition assessment the relevant markets were considered to be: 1. the local market for the retail sale of packaged liquor for off premises consumption. The geographic dimension of this market was considered to be approximated by a 3-6 kilometre radius surrounding the target business. (Market 1); 2. the local market for the supply of goods by supermarkets. The geographic dimension of this market was considered to be approximated by a 3-6 kilometre radius surrounding the target business. (Market 2); 3. the NSW market for the wholesale supply of packaged liquor for subsequent sale in the retail market for off-premises consumption (Market 3); and 4. The NSW market(s) for the procurement of products sold in supermarkets (Market 4).
body_sections.Competition analysis: The ACCC formed the view that the proposed acquisition is unlikely to substantially lessen competition in the relevant markets for the following reasons: 1. In relation to Market 1, if a 3-5 km radius around the target business is adopted, the acquisition represents a bare transfer of market share, since Woolworths has no liquor outlets within 5km of the target. If a wider geographic market definition were adopted (6km), which would include another Woolworths outlet, the ACCC concluded that competition from Coles and a number of independent hotels will provide a competitive constraint on Woolworths post-acquisition; 2. In relation to Market 2, while Woolworths will own two stores in the local market post-acquisition, it will continue to face competition from a number of competitors, including a Coles and an ALDI store as well as independents, which are likely to constrain Woolworths post-acquisition; 3. In relation to Markets 3 and 4, the ACCC considered that the acquisition of one retail store is unlikely to significantly increase Woolworths' market share (or buying power) in either market.
